PROJECT PLAN 
VoicePilot 
An AI-Powered Voice Assistant for Desktop Task Automation 
DA598A – Introduction to Generative AI 
Richmond Boakye 
Individual project

1. Project Title 
VoicePilot – An AI-Powered Voice Assistant for Desktop Task Automation 
2. Group Member(s) 
Richmond Boakye – Individual project 
3. Objective 
The objective is to build a browser-based voice assistant that lets a user control a small, safe set of desktop tasks 
using natural spoken language. The application will capture speech, convert it to text, interpret the user’s intention 
with an AI model, and execute an approved action through a Python backend. It is intended for students, developers 
and other computer users who want a simple hands-free way to perform repetitive tasks such as opening an 
application, searching the web, creating a note, or recalling previously saved information. The project will

repetitive tasks such as opening an 
application, searching the web, creating a note, or recalling previously saved information. The project will 
demonstrate speech processing, LLM-based intent understanding, prompt design, conversation memory, data 
preprocessing and frontend/backend integration. 
4. Application Features 
• Voice input and transcription: Record a short command in the browser and transcribe it using a speech-to-text 
model. 
• Intent understanding: Use an LLM to convert natural-language commands into a small structured action 
format, for example OPEN_APP, WEB_SEARCH, CREATE_NOTE or RECALL_MEMORY. 
• Safe desktop actions: Execute only allow-listed actions such as opening selected applications/folders, opening a 
web search and creating a text note.

desktop actions: Execute only allow-listed actions such as opening selected applications/folders, opening a 
web search and creating a text note. 
• Conversation memory: Store recent interactions and selected user notes so follow-up requests can use previous 
context. 
• Response generation: Return a short natural-language confirmation or explanation after an action is interpreted 
or completed. 
• Browser interface: Provide a simple React/TypeScript interface showing microphone status, transcript, detected 
intent, action result and conversation history. 
• Validation and error handling: Reject unknown or unsafe actions and show clear feedback when speech or 
intent recognition fails.

5. Source of Data 
The main project dataset will be a small raw voice-command dataset created for the project. I will record multiple 
variations of commands for each supported action, for example “Open Visual Studio Code”, “Start VS Code”, and 
“I want to code”. Each audio sample will be paired with a target intent label and, where relevant, an entity such as 
the application name or search query. 
The raw data will require preprocessing before it is used. The planned preprocessing includes removing empty or 
unusable recordings, speech-to-text transcription, text normalization, duplicate checking, intent labeling, and 
splitting the samples into development/test groups. The processed data will be used to evaluate how reliably the

checking, intent labeling, and 
splitting the samples into development/test groups. The processed data will be used to evaluate how reliably the 
assistant maps different natural-language expressions to the correct intent. A pretrained speech model will be used 
rather than training speech recognition from scratch. 
If additional examples are needed, I may extend the dataset with manually written paraphrases of the supported 
commands, while keeping the original recorded samples as the primary raw source. 
6. Intended Tech Stack 
• Frontend: React, TypeScript, Vite, HTML/CSS and browser microphone APIs. 
• Backend: Python, FastAPI and Uvicorn. 
• Speech-to-text: Whisper or faster-whisper.

TypeScript, Vite, HTML/CSS and browser microphone APIs. 
• Backend: Python, FastAPI and Uvicorn. 
• Speech-to-text: Whisper or faster-whisper. 
• LLM / language understanding: A small pretrained model accessed locally through Hugging Face or Ollama, 
with prompt refinement and structured output for intent detection. 
• Memory / persistence: SQLite for conversation history, saved notes and basic application state. 
• Desktop integration: Python standard libraries such as os, subprocess, pathlib and webbrowser, restricted to 
predefined allow-listed actions. 
• Development and testing: Visual Studio Code, Git/GitHub, Postman or FastAPI Swagger for API testing, and 
pytest where appropriate.

Planned Project Scope 
To keep the project feasible, the first version will support a limited set of approximately five to seven desktop 
intents rather than unrestricted computer control. The focus will be on a complete working pipeline: speech input → 
transcription → AI intent interpretation → validated action → response. Additional actions or text-to-speech output 
will be treated as optional extensions after the core functions are stable.
